note: Staged editorial draft only; a verified and independently reviewed PDF must be registered in MAIC before bank review/activation. Not an active exam.

questions.stem: Which action best represents journalism?
options: Verify a public-interest question using appropriate evidence
Republish a press release without checking it
Make an eyewitness quotation sound more fluent
Choose a headline only from audience reactions
questions.rationale: Journalism examines evidence before presenting claims. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Journalism, page 2.

questions.stem: Why should a beginner distinguish facts from interpretations?
options: Readers need to know what is established and what is inferred
Interpretations are always more reliable than records
Facts do not require any source
A reader can never distinguish those categories
questions.rationale: The manual teaches careful separation of evidence and inference. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Journalism, page 2.

questions.stem: Which objective belongs to this introductory course?
options: Produce advertising without disclosure
Write and check a short attributed news report
Replace sources with generated dialogue
Claim an academic qualification after reading
questions.rationale: The learning outcomes include producing verified, clearly attributed reports. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Journalism, page 2.

questions.stem: What does a reporting process need to be accountable?
options: Only a finished image file
Notes and source details sufficient to reconstruct claims
Only a preferred headline
Only a sponsor's written approval
questions.rationale: An evidence trail enables review and corrections. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Journalism, page 2.

questions.stem: Why can an appealing news story still be unsuitable for publication?
options: It has too few dramatic adjectives
Its subject is a local service
It includes a dated primary source
Its central allegation may not be verified
questions.rationale: Engagement does not outweigh the requirement for accuracy. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Journalism, page 2.

questions.stem: How should a learner use the fictional exercises?
options: Practice identifying evidence without portraying examples as actual events
Submit the invented people as verified interview sources
Treat every scenario as a current news report
Publish simulated claims as confirmed facts
questions.rationale: Training scenarios are explicitly fictional. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Journalism, page 2.

questions.stem: What makes a journalistic question useful to residents?
options: It creates maximum emotional pressure
A verifiable answer could inform their decisions
It has no relation to a public need
It cannot be answered from any source
questions.rationale: Useful reporting serves a specific information need. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Journalism, page 2.

questions.stem: Why are journalistic facts checked independently?
options: Because statements can be sincere and still be incomplete or wrong
Because every witness deliberately lies
Because primary records never contain mistakes
Because emotional confidence confirms truth
questions.rationale: Verification tests the claim rather than the speaker's confidence. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Journalism, page 2.

questions.stem: What is a suitable outcome of an introductory self-check?
options: Automatic eligibility for a degree
Permission to invent missing sources
Identifying which reporting skills need further practice
A claim of completed independent academic review
questions.rationale: Self-assessment is practice rather than formal certification. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Journalism, page 2.

questions.stem: Which sequence most closely matches responsible reporting?
options: Question, evidence, check, contextualize, publish and correct if needed
Headline, invent quotes, publish, then seek sources
Accept claims, add photographs, omit attribution
Publish first and reject subsequent evidence
questions.rationale: The process builds from inquiry through checked publication. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Journalism, page 2.

questions.stem: What makes a transport timetable change potentially newsworthy?
options: It necessarily produces national controversy
It guarantees higher advertising revenue
It affects travelers who need accurate practical information
It must involve a famous public figure
questions.rationale: Timely service changes can be useful to a defined audience. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Journalism, page 3.

questions.stem: Which is a neutral news question?
options: Why has management ruined the library?
When does the new library schedule begin and which services change?
Who is certainly responsible for every problem?
How can the notice sound more alarming?
questions.rationale: Neutral questions can be checked against actual announcements. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Journalism, page 3.

questions.stem: What is a risk of writing a dramatic headline before checking the record?
options: It guarantees better investigation
It makes source identification unnecessary
It can bias which evidence the reporter accepts
It prevents conflicting accounts
questions.rationale: Premature framing can steer the reporting. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Journalism, page 3.

questions.stem: Which detail is critical to a report about extended weekend opening?
options: The reporter's preferred font
The exact start date and hours in the official notice
The number of likes on an unrelated post
The reader's favorite book genre
questions.rationale: Practical schedule details deliver public value. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Journalism, page 3.

questions.stem: Which news value describes the extent of effects on people?
options: Paragraph length
Impact
Brand loyalty
Webpage theme
questions.rationale: Impact considers who is affected and how. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Journalism, page 3.

questions.stem: How should a reporter handle an appealing but unverified claim?
options: Publish it as a fact because it is unusual
Treat repost counts as evidence
Investigate it and identify its current uncertainty
Remove contradictory source information
questions.rationale: Unverified claims should not be presented as established. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Journalism, page 3.

questions.stem: Why should a story proposal name its intended audience?
options: An audience definition proves the story true
It guarantees the source will cooperate
It replaces identifying missing facts
Different readers need different relevant information
questions.rationale: Audience relevance helps shape the reporting question. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Journalism, page 3.

questions.stem: What is inappropriate about claiming a temporary service is permanent?
options: It is acceptable because the word is shorter
It is a harmless stylistic choice
It becomes true if widely shared
It overstates the scope established by the source
questions.rationale: Headlines must match the supported timeframe. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Journalism, page 3.

questions.stem: When should a journalist amend a proposed news angle?
options: When verified evidence changes the understanding of events
Whenever the first headline gets few likes
Only after an advertiser requests a change
Never once the pitch is written
questions.rationale: The investigation should follow evidence. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Journalism, page 3.

questions.stem: What should a beginner's story proposal include?
options: Only a promotional slogan
Only an accusation against a named person
Only an attractive photograph
Public relevance, sources and a testable central question
questions.rationale: A reporting plan needs purpose and verifiability. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Journalism, page 3.

questions.stem: What distinguishes an allegation from an established fact?
options: The allegation must always be false
The allegation cannot be quoted with attribution
The allegation is a claim that has not yet been adequately verified
The fact is whatever the loudest person says
questions.rationale: Evidence and attribution determine the supported status. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Journalism, page 4.

questions.stem: What does a signed proposal show without further records?
options: Full implementation is complete
All spending has been approved
A proposal exists, not necessarily an adopted policy
Every affected person agrees
questions.rationale: Document status controls the conclusion. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Journalism, page 4.

questions.stem: Which is an example of an opinion?
options: The new service is the best improvement in years
The notice is dated 18 November
The posted opening hour is 9 a.m.
The council voted in a recorded meeting
questions.rationale: Evaluative judgments differ from verifiable recorded details. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Journalism, page 4.

questions.stem: What is a forecast?
options: A statement about a possible future result
A completed transaction
A firsthand observation of past events
An authenticated photograph
questions.rationale: Forecasts express future expectations rather than established outcomes. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Journalism, page 4.

questions.stem: A school has authorized funding for computers. What remains unproven?
options: That the computers have been physically delivered
That a funding decision took place
That the proposal covered equipment
That the council considered the issue
questions.rationale: Approval does not demonstrate fulfillment. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Journalism, page 4.

questions.stem: Why is the word according to useful when accurately applied?
options: It converts every allegation into fact
It removes a need to read the underlying document
It proves all reported causes
It identifies the source supporting the reported assertion
questions.rationale: Source attribution clarifies who states a claim. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Journalism, page 4.

questions.stem: Which statement is justified by a dated meeting agenda alone?
options: The proposal passed unanimously
All the work has been completed
The plan was permanently funded
The proposal appears on the agenda
questions.rationale: An agenda alone does not establish decisions. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Journalism, page 4.

questions.stem: How should journalists report an unknown cause?
options: State a likely cause as certain
Describe verified effects while noting the cause is unconfirmed
Infer the cause solely from public anger
Invent a specialist quotation
questions.rationale: Transparent uncertainty prevents invented explanations. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Journalism, page 4.

questions.stem: A witness reports a single late bus. What broader claim is not yet established?
options: That the witness experienced a delay
That every bus on the route is routinely late
That a bus route exists
That the witness made a statement
questions.rationale: A single observation cannot establish a system-wide pattern. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Journalism, page 4.

questions.stem: Why distinguish a quote of an assertion from endorsement of it?
options: Reporting what was said does not automatically verify its content
All quoted words must be true
Quotes are exempt from contextual checking
Attribution allows inventing missing records
questions.rationale: Quotation and independent verification are separate. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Journalism, page 4.

questions.stem: What should a reporter assess about an expert source?
options: How many followers the expert has alone
Whether expertise applies to the particular claim
Whether the expert agrees with the headline
Only how confidently the expert speaks
questions.rationale: Source relevance is claim-specific. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Journalism, page 5.

questions.stem: Why are two websites copying one rumor not two confirmations?
options: They derive from a single unverified origin
The web addresses are different
The articles use different fonts
The sites have different publication times
questions.rationale: Independent corroboration requires independent evidence. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Journalism, page 5.

questions.stem: What best documents a proposed claim during investigation?
options: A claim-source-status table with unresolved questions
A draft headline with no references
A collection of unrelated screenshots
Only a tally of social views
questions.rationale: A source table exposes verification status. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Journalism, page 5.

questions.stem: A notice announces a planned opening. What does it establish?
options: The institution announced the plan
The opening has already occurred
All services are permanently available
Residents have attended the opening
questions.rationale: An announcement need not prove completion. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Journalism, page 5.

questions.stem: Why check an original notice rather than an isolated screenshot?
options: All screenshots are false
The image may omit amendments or important context
Only printed media can provide evidence
An image cannot include accurate words
questions.rationale: Original context clarifies document status and meaning. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Journalism, page 5.

questions.stem: What should a reporter do when official and ticketing attendance numbers differ?
options: Choose the larger number without explanation
Clarify counting definitions before selecting a figure
Take the average automatically
Describe the figures as identical
questions.rationale: Different metrics can yield different legitimate counts. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Journalism, page 5.

questions.stem: When should a firsthand witness be used for a regional statistic?
options: Only with appropriate supporting population-level evidence
Whenever the witness seems sincere
Whenever the post has many likes
When the witness declines to supply records
questions.rationale: One experience is not automatically representative. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Journalism, page 5.

questions.stem: What is a primary record for a council vote?
options: A generic marketing campaign
An unlinked anonymous comment
The authenticated minutes or official recorded decision
An unrelated stock photograph
questions.rationale: Primary records directly document formal decisions. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Journalism, page 5.

questions.stem: Why record the date of each source document?
options: Its relevance and accuracy may change with revisions
Dates are only design elements
An old version is always definitive
The date confirms all predictions
questions.rationale: Version and timing are essential evidence context. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Journalism, page 5.

questions.stem: How should conflicting credible accounts be presented when unresolved?
options: Invent a compromise quotation
Ignore the less convenient account
Identify the disputed point and evidence limits
Describe one as false without checking
questions.rationale: Disagreement should be described with transparent support. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Journalism, page 5.

questions.stem: Which field note is a direct observation?
options: The city must be hiding an accident
A barrier was visible outside the station at 9:15 a.m.
Every driver was negligent
The delays will continue indefinitely
questions.rationale: Direct observation records what the reporter actually saw. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Journalism, page 6.

questions.stem: What is the problem with the question Why did you intentionally neglect residents?
options: It requests a date
It leaves room for several explanations
It embeds a contested accusation in the wording
It identifies a document for checking
questions.rationale: Neutral questions avoid assuming a disputed motive. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Journalism, page 6.

questions.stem: What should an interviewer ask after an uncertain date is mentioned?
options: May we replace it with a more interesting date?
Can we treat the estimate as exact?
Should the article omit all dates?
Can you confirm the date from a record or calendar?
questions.rationale: Specific follow-up improves accuracy. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Journalism, page 6.

questions.stem: What should a source be told at the beginning of an interview?
options: Who the journalist is and the intended reporting purpose
That every reply must be favorable
That recording is always permitted in every location
That the source cannot request clarification
questions.rationale: Transparent purpose supports ethical interviewing. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Journalism, page 6.

questions.stem: Why is it inappropriate to infer an official cause from seeing a barrier?
options: Barriers can never be observed accurately
Official records are never useful
The reporter already knows all causes
The observed object does not establish why it was installed
questions.rationale: Evidence for a cause differs from evidence of a condition. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Journalism, page 6.

questions.stem: What should be preserved for accurate quotation?
options: Only a polished paraphrase
Original notes or recordings subject to suitable safeguards
Only the source's preferred headline
Only the shortest possible quote
questions.rationale: Original records support later verification. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Journalism, page 6.

questions.stem: What should a reporter do after an ambiguous technical term in an interview?
options: Replace it with an invented synonym
Ask for clarification and verify its spelling and meaning
Omit attribution entirely
Assume transcription software is perfect
questions.rationale: Technical misunderstandings can materially change a story. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Journalism, page 6.

questions.stem: Which approach is preferable with a distressed interviewee?
options: Press for the most dramatic retelling
Provide clear communication and avoid coercive repetition
Publish unnecessary personal information
Ignore appropriate consent expectations
questions.rationale: Vulnerable sources require sensitive treatment. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Journalism, page 6.

questions.stem: How should an interviewer deal with a source who declines comment?
options: Treat refusal as admission of wrongdoing
Write a hypothetical quote under their name
Record the refusal accurately without inventing an explanation
Delete the original question from all records
questions.rationale: A refusal does not establish a cause. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Journalism, page 6.

questions.stem: Why should time and place be recorded alongside interview material?
options: They replace checking the words spoken
They support identification and contextual validation of the account
They guarantee the source is independent
They make all private details publishable
questions.rationale: Provenance matters for source reliability. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Journalism, page 6.

questions.stem: What is the role of a news lead?
options: Include every historical detail before the news
Hide the current change until the final paragraph
Start with the most dramatic unsupported accusation
Present the essential verified development early
questions.rationale: The lead prioritizes the main established fact. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Journalism, page 7.

questions.stem: What is the inverted pyramid?
options: An approach that puts important facts before less essential detail
A requirement to end with the only verified detail
A method of placing ads above news
A plan to avoid source attribution
questions.rationale: The structure supports rapid understanding. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Journalism, page 7.

questions.stem: What does the W in who ask?
options: The report's word count
The website name only
The people or organization involved
The width of a photograph
questions.rationale: Who identifies relevant actors. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Journalism, page 7.

questions.stem: What if the why of an event has not been verified?
options: State known circumstances without inventing a cause
Make the most plausible cause categorical
Assume the first witness knows the full reason
Omit all other verified details
questions.rationale: The five Ws do not justify speculation. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Journalism, page 7.

questions.stem: Which lead fits a planned weekend-opening trial?
options: The library has permanently expanded all services
The city ordered every school to open on Sunday
The library will test Sunday opening beginning next month, according to its notice
The library already served record crowds today
questions.rationale: A lead must preserve planned status and source. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Journalism, page 7.

questions.stem: Why should background usually follow the main verified development?
options: Historic context is never useful
The beginning may contain any invented fact
Readers first need to understand what changed
A lead must include every quote
questions.rationale: Story structure prioritizes consequence and clarity. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Journalism, page 7.

questions.stem: What does a direct quote contribute most appropriately?
options: Proof that the story needs no corroboration
A replacement for every numerical check
Source-specific evidence or perspective with accurate attribution
A guarantee that the reported claim is true
questions.rationale: Quotations add evidence but do not independently prove all content. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Journalism, page 7.

questions.stem: How should chronology be managed in a story?
options: Describe every future plan as completed
Use a different event date in each paragraph
Keep planned, current and completed events distinct
Remove dates to reduce precision
questions.rationale: Temporal accuracy is part of a coherent report. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Journalism, page 7.

questions.stem: Which paragraph is most useful after a verified library-hours lead?
options: A speculative history of unrelated institutions
The exact opening dates and services available
A source's unverified personal accusation
An unrelated product advertisement
questions.rationale: Follow-up details should answer the reader's practical questions. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Journalism, page 7.

questions.stem: Why may a beginner choose inverted-pyramid reporting for a short announcement?
options: It removes the need for verification
It guarantees every headline is legally safe
It makes central facts accessible even if readers stop early
It prevents the use of original records
questions.rationale: A clear order improves service-news readability. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Journalism, page 7.

questions.stem: What is wrong with a headline saying Council builds lanes based on an agenda item?
options: The headline contains a location
The sentence is short
The agenda shows consideration, not completed construction
The subject is public infrastructure
questions.rationale: A headline must match the recorded status. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Journalism, page 8.

questions.stem: What do quotation marks around an interview statement signify?
options: They indicate an approximate paraphrase
They prove the words are true
They permit invented speech in context
They represent the person's actual words
questions.rationale: Quotes require fidelity to recorded speech. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Journalism, page 8.

questions.stem: Why must a reporter check captions for old file photographs?
options: Archive photos are always prohibited
A caption cannot contain factual assertions
Image date never affects interpretation
Readers may mistake them for images of the current event
questions.rationale: Caption provenance prevents temporal misrepresentation. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Journalism, page 8.

questions.stem: What is an appropriate way to shorten a quotation?
options: Remove all qualifiers that weaken the point
Combine sentences from different speakers
Remove nonessential words without changing its meaning
Add the reporter's wording inside quote marks
questions.rationale: Editing must preserve substantive meaning. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Journalism, page 8.

questions.stem: Which wording is appropriate for a not-yet-approved proposal?
options: The council has completed the project
The proposal is permanently operating
The council is considering the proposal
The plan has already achieved its results
questions.rationale: Status words convey the difference between proposal and implementation. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Journalism, page 8.

questions.stem: An arrest is reported but no verdict exists. Which headline is unwarranted?
options: Court convicts suspect of the alleged crime
Police report an arrest in the investigation
Authorities say an arrest was made
Investigation continues after arrest
questions.rationale: Arrest and conviction are separate legal stages. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Journalism, page 8.

questions.stem: What makes a headline accurate?
options: It receives the most views
It uses the strongest possible verbs
Every significant assertion is supported by the article's evidence
It omits all qualifications
questions.rationale: Headlines are factual statements requiring support. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Journalism, page 8.

questions.stem: What should a caption do when an image is illustrative rather than from the event?
options: Let viewers infer it was taken today
Clearly identify it as an illustrative or file image
Include a fabricated eyewitness location
Remove any relevant date
questions.rationale: Labeling prevents false documentary inference. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Journalism, page 8.

questions.stem: A recorded source says service might expand. Which paraphrase is fair?
options: The source confirmed expansion was complete
The source promised permanent expansion
The source denied any potential change
The source said an expansion was possible
questions.rationale: Paraphrase must preserve uncertainty and scope. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Journalism, page 8.

questions.stem: Why should journalists avoid changing a quote into more fluent invented language?
options: It attributes words to someone who did not say them
Grammar is more important than source accuracy
It is required for short articles
Verbatim speech is never usable
questions.rationale: Journalistic quotations must represent actual speech. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Journalism, page 8.

questions.stem: What can make an otherwise true article misleading?
options: Any mention of a date
Omission of necessary context or counterevidence
An attributed statement
A short paragraph structure
questions.rationale: Whole-story accuracy includes context. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Journalism, page 9.

questions.stem: What should a newsroom do with a material published numerical error?
options: Hide the corrected figure only in internal records
Keep the wrong figure if engagement was high
Correct the figure promptly and explain the change
Describe both numbers as equally accurate
questions.rationale: Visible corrections maintain accountability. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Journalism, page 9.

questions.stem: Why must sponsored content be labeled?
options: To guarantee the sponsor's statements are true
To exempt it from any laws
To remove all editorial review
To prevent commercial messages being mistaken for independent reporting
questions.rationale: Transparency reveals commercial influence. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Journalism, page 9.

questions.stem: What is fair response to a serious allegation?
options: Give the accused person control of every published fact
Seek a relevant reply when feasible and report material evidence accurately
Ignore the underlying documents
Publish an invented denial if no reply arrives
questions.rationale: Fairness permits response without requiring false balance. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Journalism, page 9.

questions.stem: What is an important privacy question before publishing a witness's address?
options: Will the address attract more clicks?
Can the address fit in the headline?
Is disclosure necessary for public understanding and proportionate to harm?
Does the witness own a social account?
questions.rationale: An accurate private detail may still pose unjustified risk. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Journalism, page 9.

questions.stem: How should a correction for 41 versus 14 permits be written?
options: Both counts are equally correct without explanation
The numerical difference is merely stylistic
No correction is needed when the subject is local
The earlier figure was incorrect; the verified figure is 14
questions.rationale: Corrections should identify exactly what changed. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Journalism, page 9.

questions.stem: What is a conflict of interest in reporting?
options: A reporter verifying two sources
A person declining an interview
A factual headline referencing a public notice
A financial relationship that could affect independent editorial judgment
questions.rationale: Competing private incentives may threaten independence. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Journalism, page 9.

questions.stem: Why should strong evidence and unsupported denial not receive equal weight?
options: All disputes must be split evenly
Official statements cannot ever be questioned
False equivalence can mislead readers about the strength of support
Factual accuracy requires choosing the most popular view
questions.rationale: Evidence strength should guide presentation. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Journalism, page 9.

questions.stem: When may specialist review be especially appropriate?
options: Whenever a source uses a long sentence
Before publishing high-risk legal or sensitive allegations
Only for sports news
Whenever a caption is short
questions.rationale: Greater potential harm requires proportionate review. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Journalism, page 9.

questions.stem: Which behavior best supports correction-ready journalism?
options: Delete all past published versions silently
Record only the latest headline
Preserve the original sources and a revision history
Avoid documenting any changed number
questions.rationale: Traceability makes corrections more credible. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Journalism, page 9.

questions.stem: Why should a viral post not be treated as verified just because it has many views?
options: View counts are always fake
Only national outlets can publish truth
High views are proof of an eyewitness
Popularity does not establish source accuracy
questions.rationale: Independent evidence is still necessary. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Journalism, page 10.

questions.stem: What should a journalist check about a supposed current stadium-fire image?
options: Original event, date, place and subsequent repost context
Only whether flames look realistic
Only how many emojis accompany it
Only which filter makes it more dramatic
questions.rationale: An old real photo can be miscaptioned as current. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Journalism, page 10.

questions.stem: What is a valid use of AI transcription?
options: Draft notes that are checked against the actual audio
Create a quotation not present in the recording
Add a missing interview subject
Convert uncertain numbers into exact results
questions.rationale: AI-assisted output needs original-source verification. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Journalism, page 10.

questions.stem: How should a short caption handle a tentative estimate?
options: Remove the qualifier for brevity
Preserve that the quantity is estimated
Describe it as audited fact
Replace it with an invented larger figure
questions.rationale: Format length does not remove meaningful uncertainty. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Journalism, page 10.

questions.stem: What should the term sponsored identify?
options: Content supported or paid for by an advertiser
An independent newsroom correction
A verified eyewitness account
A public agenda
questions.rationale: Labels help distinguish promotional from editorial content. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Journalism, page 10.

questions.stem: Why check where a photo first appeared?
options: The first post is always true
Photo origins never matter to location
It proves every subsequent caption accurate
It helps establish provenance and whether it matches the claimed event
questions.rationale: Original context may reveal repurposing. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Journalism, page 10.

questions.stem: What is wrong with declaring a claim true based only on online engagement?
options: All popular stories are intentionally false
Engagement is not independent factual corroboration
Only unpopular claims can be news
Engagement is the same as an official record
questions.rationale: Public reaction cannot substitute for evidence. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Journalism, page 10.

questions.stem: How should multimedia summaries relate to a full verified article?
options: Preserve its core facts and important qualifications
Replace cautious words with categorical claims
Discard relevant source attribution
Invent material omitted from the original
questions.rationale: Short formats must remain faithful to evidence. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Journalism, page 10.

questions.stem: When should a reporter challenge an AI-generated summary?
options: Only when the style is dull
Never when the output is grammatically polished
Only after it is reposted
When it contains a detail absent from the original source
questions.rationale: Generated details must be checked against actual evidence. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Journalism, page 10.

questions.stem: What is the first step when verifying a suspicious 15-second clip?
options: Select a headline based on reactions
Assume the uploader has permission to identify victims
Treat every visible person as a verified witness
Seek the original footage and relevant context
questions.rationale: Video provenance is essential before assigning time and place. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Journalism, page 10.

questions.stem: What does the fictional library notice establish?
options: The library has permanently shifted to seven-day opening
Every facility is available all week
A six-week experiment in Sunday opening is planned
The experiment has already been evaluated
questions.rationale: The scenario describes a temporary trial, not a permanent change. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Journalism, page 11.

questions.stem: Why is the social post claiming permanent opening unsupported?
options: It names the correct institution
It was posted on a social network
It uses the word library
It extends a six-week plan into an indefinite commitment
questions.rationale: The source notice does not support permanence. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Journalism, page 11.

questions.stem: What is an appropriate source for the planned start date?
options: An unrelated social argument
The dated original library notice
An anonymous prediction about future budgets
An old file photograph of the building
questions.rationale: The original notice states the schedule. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Journalism, page 11.

questions.stem: Which service status is left unanswered by the case facts?
options: Whether ordinary borrowing is announced
Whether computer rooms are available during Sunday opening
Whether the notice is temporary
Whether it was published by the library
questions.rationale: The scenario specifically leaves ancillary services unresolved. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Journalism, page 11.

questions.stem: What should the reporter do if the library has not responded about room bookings?
options: State the question remains unconfirmed rather than inventing an answer
Write that the rooms definitely remain open
Claim the library refused to provide any services
Assume that permanent booking policies changed
questions.rationale: No response does not establish an operational fact. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Journalism, page 11.

questions.stem: Which lead accurately describes the fictional case?
options: The library now operates permanently seven days a week
The library has closed all Sunday services
The library's budget was permanently increased
The library will test Sunday opening for six weeks next month
questions.rationale: The verified notice concerns a temporary opening trial. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Journalism, page 11.

questions.stem: What should a claim-source matrix show about the permanent-opening assertion?
options: It is fully proven by the social post
It should be used as the main headline
It needs no follow-up because it is popular
The source notice does not verify it
questions.rationale: A matrix exposes unsupported extrapolation. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Journalism, page 11.

questions.stem: What action is necessary if a published opening date is wrong?
options: Leave it uncorrected until the six-week trial ends
Remove all mention of the library
Replace it with a speculative time range silently
Correct the public-facing date and document the change
questions.rationale: A date affects readers' ability to use the service. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Journalism, page 11.

questions.stem: Why should borrowing-service information be included in the story?
options: It proves computer rooms are open
It guarantees permanent Sunday opening
It makes the start date irrelevant
It helps residents know what is actually available
questions.rationale: Practical public-service details are newsworthy. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Journalism, page 11.

questions.stem: What is the central editorial lesson of the library exercise?
options: Choose whichever social-media claim is most popular
Treat all scheduled changes as completed
Avoid asking the institution for clarification
Report exactly what the notice supports and label remaining uncertainties
questions.rationale: The worked case trains boundary-setting between evidence and inference. Source: MAIC Fundamentals of Journalism, page 11.
